assessment.reason: The model and a two-book market roughly agree, and the +159 price sits slightly above both. The margin is thin but has no identified material blocker.
assessment.model_case: The model projects about 0.93 made threes with a median of 1, so it expects roughly one make. Modest variance in a center's attempt rate decides this binary line, so a small shift in volume could flip the case.
assessment.price_case: At +159, break-even is about 39 in 100 on a main 0.5 line. The model and the two-book reference sit just above that. The edge is narrow and sensitive to small errors in the three-point attempt rate.
assessment.context_case: No source addresses Clingan's role or status; context is unverified. The Portland injury listings concern guards and wings, not Clingan directly.

qualitative_review.countercase: A center's three-point attempts can swing with matchup and coaching choices. If Minnesota's frontcourt alignment or Portland's guard absences raise his perimeter looks, the under's narrow margin disappears. The model and market sit too close together to call this a distinct edge.

assessment.reason: Toronto's listed center absence could raise Murray-Boyles' rebounding chances beyond what a model without teammate adjustments assumes, and Knicks injury coverage is missing.
assessment.model_case: Projected 5.94 rebounds with a median of 6 over 29.1 minutes, against a 6.5 line. The cushion is under one rebound, and the gap over the five-book market may come from ignoring frontcourt absences rather than from real information.
assessment.price_case: At -112 on the main 6.5 line, break-even is about 53 in 100. Five books give a sturdier reference, and the market sits closer to break-even than the model does.
assessment.context_case: Bittle's listed absence leaves Toronto thinner at center. The New York side of the injury table is missing, so the opposing frontcourt's rebounding is unknown.
blocking_checks: Knicks injury report: whether New York's frontcourt rebounders are active changes how many boards are available, which directly moves the under.
Whether the rolling sample already includes games without Bittle; if not, the projection likely understates rebounding opportunity.

qualitative_review.countercase: If recent games already reflect Bittle's absence and New York's frontcourt is fully active, the projection may hold and the under remains plausible. Even so, the gap over a five-book market deserves skepticism.

Lakers' Collin Sexton: Questionable to play Sunday

findings.note: Sexton now plays for the Lakers, averaging 2.6 APG. He had 3, 3, 6, 2 and 1 assists in his last five games, clearing 2.5 in three. He was cleared from a head cut and played 24 minutes at Phoenix on Nov 15.

Nov 14 report: Sexton (head) was questionable after needing stitches but practiced fully. He averaged 2.6 assists over his previous five games. His minutes ranged from 11 to 27, which leaves the result sensitive to his minutes.

Sexton is expected to back up Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, which limits his ball-handling. The page's news feed also lists several recent RotoWire 'ruled out' items for him with unclear dates, so his status for this game should be checked.

ESPN's 2026-27 team leaders list Cunningham at 25.7 points per game in 34.7 minutes on 47.7% shooting. That average is above the 23.5 line, though his career-high 52-point game against Washington pushes it up.

RotoWire's game log shows he swings a lot from game to game. He scored 16, 22, 19, 20 and 14 points in some games and 26, 30, 33 and 52 in others. Before the 52-point game he averaged 15.5 points over two games. No injury or status news for Nov 17 was found.

From last season: Cunningham went 5-for-26 for 16 points in a loss to the Spurs. Another loss to San Antonio last season, also on CBS, saw him score 26 points on 10-for-26 shooting, so his results against them are mixed.
